events.what: Cocos's arXiv:1504.04852, dormant since 2015 and then revised v4–v12 (31 March to 6 December 2025), now claims a proof of Chern's conjecture for closed flat affine manifolds
events.credibility_reason: F5: several signals together. (1) Misread scope: an affine manifold carries a flat, torsion-free connection by definition, so 'flat affine manifolds' is the whole conjecture, a landmark claim where two earlier full proofs (Feng–Zhang 2016, Ge 2020) were retracted. (2) The claim's own history: a 2015 preprint dormant for a decade, then nine major revisions in nine months in 2025, which the author's own AMS Fall 2025 abstract calls 'A posible proof'. (3) No uptake: no journal acceptance and no expert discussion found. The one citing paper (arXiv:2510.09648) treats it only as 'evidence for Chern's conjecture', and the live Wikipedia article still calls the conjecture unsolved and does not mention it. The first written argument may date from 2015 (v1), which is before the snapshot; it makes no difference, because the claim is discarded either way.

judgement.doubts: The scope is 'whole', not a sub-case, because an affine manifold is flat by definition. That makes the claim a full proof of a famous conjecture, with no expert uptake and with the author's own hedging. The Feng–Zhang and Ge retractions both predate the snapshot and resolved nothing, so the status is open, not open_stale. no_change_found was left false because a discarded event was still found. I did not change credited_humans or event: the record's evidence stays in place.

corrections.why: F5: the record's own summary shows several signals together. The 2015 preprint was dormant for a decade and then revised nine times in 2025. The author's AMS abstract calls it 'A posible proof'. The only citing paper (arXiv:2510.09648) calls it merely 'evidence'. The live Wikipedia article still calls the conjecture unsolved and does not mention the claim. The record also misreads 'flat affine manifolds' as a sub-case, when an affine manifold is flat by definition, so this is an unendorsed claim to the whole conjecture. The event is discarded, and nothing else survives.
